idiom_name: Spring for Apache Kafka @KafkaListener (JVM listener container)
implementation_notes: Kotlin consumes the JVM messaging stack, so the endpoint is the framework's listener: an @KafkaListener/@RabbitListener-annotated method is wrapped in a listener container that owns the consumer, concurrency and acknowledgement mode, and the function body only maps payloads to domain calls. Kotlin's coroutines are not integrated with a messaging runtime (there is no official coroutines JMS module), so a suspending consumer requires adapting the container's callback into a Channel/Flow yourself; the classic hand-written endpoint remains justified only when no container framework is used.
pitfalls: Listener methods run on container threads, not on coroutines: launching fire-and-forget coroutines inside the handler breaks back-pressure and can acknowledge the offset before the work completes.

Kotlin's default final classes and null-safety do not protect the callback: a thrown exception inside the listener triggers the container's error handler, so map domain errors to explicit handling instead of letting them escape.
Annotation attributes are strings/SpEL resolved at runtime: a typo in a topic or group id fails at startup or silently subscribes elsewhere, so assert the wiring in a test.
